draft.title: General adaptation syndrome
card: General adaptation syndrome (GAS) is Hans Selye's model of how the body responds to a long-lasting stressor. It has three stages in a set order.
Alarm reaction
the body first goes into shock, and resistance to the stressor drops. Then countershock follows, as the body starts to fight back and arousal rises.
Resistance
the body works to cope with a stressor that continues. Arousal stays raised, and the body uses up its energy to keep going.
Exhaustion
if the stressor lasts too long, the body's resources run low. Resistance falls, and the person becomes more open to illness.
draft.remember: GAS runs in order: alarm reaction, resistance, then exhaustion. Resources are used up over time.

a.q: Which description fits the resistance stage of the GAS?
opts: The body keeps coping with a stressor that is still there
The body first drops into shock when the stressor appears
The body's resources run low and illness becomes more likely
The stressor is gone and the body returns to normal
a.why: In resistance, the stressor continues and the body keeps working to cope with it. Shock belongs to the alarm reaction, and running out of resources is exhaustion.
a.clue: The stressor has not gone away, and the body is still coping.

b.q: For months, Priya has worked two jobs to pay off a debt. She now catches colds often and feels drained. Which stage is she most likely in, and why?
opts: Exhaustion, as the long stressor has used up her resources
Resistance, as her body is still coping well with the stressor
Countershock, as her body has only just begun to fight back
Alarm reaction, as she is feeling the first shock of stress
b.why: Months of stress, frequent illness and feeling drained show that her resources are running low, which is exhaustion. Resistance is tempting because the stressor continues, but in that stage the body is still coping, not wearing down.
b.clue: Look for signs that the body's resources have run low.
